neighbours.label: 'kick' in the phrasal verb 'kick off' meaning to start
fire: The mayor kicked off the festival with a short speech.
Our team will kick off the project with a planning workshop on Monday.
The conference kicks off tomorrow morning in the main hall.
We kicked off the season with a barbecue for all the volunteers.
A jazz concert will kick off the weekend celebrations downtown.
The new series kicks off with an interview with a famous chef.
She kicked off her campaign at a rally in her hometown.
Students kicked off the semester with a welcome dinner.
quiet: The mayor opened the festival with a short speech.
Our team will begin the project with a planning workshop on Monday.
The conference starts tomorrow morning in the main hall.
We launched the season with a barbecue for all the volunteers.
A jazz concert will open the weekend celebrations downtown.
The new series begins with an interview with a famous chef.
She launched her campaign at a rally in her hometown.
Students started the semester with a welcome dinner.

notes: kicked/kick/kicks before 'off' dominate; output suppresses kick/start tokens. Near misses use synonyms for 'start'.
